title: Maude deForrest, Gus Smith and the TOBA tab shows
summary: Gus Smith organizes tab shows through Indiana and Illinois on the TOBA circuit until the girls are sent home and the group returns to New York.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do you remember, what tunes were in the Plantation revue. And who else was with it. Who was with the show.

Well, we had a quartet of youngsters around there. We had Maude deForrest. Later, Maude deForrest went to Europe with Josephine Baker. She had been chosen by Josephine Baker bein' the first strip teaser. Maude deForrest was a very good blues singer. Because she had a heavy voice. And everybody thought you had to have a heavy voice to sing the blues in those days. The heavier your voice was, the better they thought you could sing the blues. As if that had anything to do with it anyway.
But they felt that way. Somebody was singing way down there, 'I Honey love you baby --', it was hoarse and raspy like that, they thought that was good, see?

And so, anyway, Maude DeForrest's partner was Gus Smith -- the guy was successful with moving. And my bunch. Then, we had a couple of comedians on the show, and the rest was -- two dancers. That's about all. But none of them of any consequence. But Gus Smith and Maude deForrest and myself, and Eddie Green, were the biggest people worth mentioning.

Anyhow, Gus organized this thing. We went about doing tab shows, because he understood all that. All down, Drake and Walker and all those. And all through Indiana and Illinois we did what you call tab shows, you know, where we got the word T-O-B-B-A from. [Theater Owners Booking Agency, aka Tough on Black Actors or Asses.]

We had a company, about 12, 15 people. And as the girls would make money, or they'd hear from home, why the show got smaller and smaller. And when it got down to where we had all the girls protected and it was all straightened out, well we went on home. Because we had money, you know what I mean? And so we went on back to New York, ourselves.
